speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I’m Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you’ve been trying to conceive and if you have any pain during intercourse?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the discomfort occur only with penetration, or do you experience pain during your menstrual periods as well? I also need to know if your menstrual cycles are regular and if you have ever had a pregnancy before.

speaker: Patient
text: he is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain with penetration and pelvic floor tension, combined with 15 months of infertility, strongly suggests endometriosis, which can cause both dyspareunia and conception difficulties. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic_Ultrasound: Normal uterus and adnexa with no evidence of fibroids or ovarian cysts.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the ultrasound is normal, we must look closer at your menstrual history to rule out ovulatory issues. Are your menstrual cycles regular, and do you experience significant pain during your periods?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Body Dysmorphic Disorder diagnosed three years ago. Social history: Does not smoke or drink alcohol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the pelvic floor tension and pain with penetration, have you experienced significant stress or anxiety related to intimacy, or is the pain strictly physical? I also need to confirm if your menstrual cycles are regular to assess for ovulatory dysfunction.

speaker: Patient
text: All other systems reviewed are within normal limits.

speaker: Doctor
text: Your history of Body Dysmorphic Disorder and the specific description of pelvic floor muscle tension suggest psychogenic dyspareunia rather than a physical pathology. DIAGNOSIS READY: Psychogenic Dyspareunia secondary to Body Dysmorphic Disorder
